o: The matrix has no inverse: its columns lie on one line
why: The second column (4, 2) is twice the first (2, 1). The matrix squashes the plane onto a line, and that can't be undone.
It's ad − bc, with a minus: 3·4 − 1·2 = 10.

q: det(A + B) = det A + det B
why: Usually false. For 2×2 matrices, I + I = 2I has determinant 4, but det I + det I = 2.
The rule is (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹, in reverse order like socks and shoes. It equals A⁻¹B⁻¹ only when those two commute.

q: Every square matrix has an inverse.
why: Myth. Only matrices with det ≠ 0 have one.
